beforeAlias.scope: Small synthetic loopback CLI comparison. UDM uses a private catalog. IDM receives only named fixture downloads; no /q, queue command, process termination or settings modification.

beforeCanonical.scope: Small synthetic loopback CLI comparison. UDM uses a private catalog. IDM receives only named fixture downloads; no /q, queue command, process termination or settings modification.

afterPaired.scope: Small synthetic loopback CLI comparison. UDM uses a private catalog. IDM receives only named fixture downloads; no /q, queue command, process termination or settings modification.

reference.scope: Installed reference executable via its CLI. Only named fixture downloads; no settings, queue-start, quit or process termination commands.

change: Normalize the x-gzip response coding to gzip before response acceptance and persistence. The existing gzip decoder, validators, saved-wire reuse and output-size projection remain responsible for the bytes.
coverage: gzip, x-gzip and mixed-case X-GZip for GET and form responses
Exact decoded size before Start equals final file size
One-response prefetch and deferred response reuse
Encoded-offset range resume with x-gzip/X-GZip initial headers and canonical gzip resumed headers
No speculative fresh form submission; exact binary form body, redirects and explicit-only restart
qualificationNotes: The initial build guard correctly stopped when the test-runner hash changed without an allowlist entry; the three intended runner changes were then included before compilation. No failed compiler result was accepted.
limits: No fresh personal-browser acceptance or dialog-paint timing comparison
Small loopback paired probe establishes functional output and request counts, not speed parity
Gzip decode still follows network completion; streaming overlap remains separate work
Deflate is not covered by the fix: IDM saved its encoded bytes in the discovery probe while UDM rejected it
No installer or installed update created
artifactPolicy: Single shared native build directory, no FFmpeg/media-tool copy. Only controlled synthetic test payloads; their hashes and removal are recorded separately.
